items.stem: A dice and a dice are used together. How many possible outcomes are there in the sample space?
Which transformation does not change the orientation of a shape?
items.markingKey: A translation slides the shape without turning or flipping. [1]

items.stem: In a class the ratio of boys to girls is 2 : 3. Freya says that 200/3% of the class are boys. Explain the mistake and give the correct percentage.
items.answer: Freya compared boys with girls, not with the whole class. Boys are 2 out of 5 parts = 40%.
items.markingKey: B1 fraction of total; B1 correct percentage. [2]

items.stem: Convert 12.5 litres to cm³.
Explain why each interior angle of a regular polygon must be less than 180°.
items.answer: Each exterior angle is 360 ÷ n, which is greater than 0, so the interior angle 180 − 360/n is less than 180°.
items.markingKey: B1 exterior > 0; B1 conclusion. [2]

items.stem: Solve 5(x + 3) = 75.
items.markingKey: Expand 5x + 15 = 75 or divide by 5 (M1); x = 12 (A1).

items.stem: Nadia is investigating whether people with longer arms also have longer legs. Which sample is likely to give the most reliable results?
options: Everyone who volunteers on the first day
A random sample of 100 from adults in the town
items.answer: A random sample of 100 from adults in the town
items.markingKey: Large and random → more representative and reliable. [1]

items.stem: Write down a whole number n so that √n is a rational number between 6 and 8.
items.markingKey: √49 = 7 is the only whole number root strictly between 6 and 8. B1 [1]

items.stem: Leila says the point (2, 5) lies on the line y = 2x. Show how to check whether Leila is right.
items.answer: Substitute x = 2: y = 2 × 2 + 0 = 4. This is not 5, so the point does not lie on the line.
items.markingKey: M1 substitution; A1 conclusion. [2]

items.stem: Use division to write 1/3 as a recurring decimal.
items.markingKey: 1.000… ÷ 3 by short division (M1); 0.333… with the repeating block identified (A1).

items.stem: Elena measured the heights, h cm, of 52 tomato plants. The results are shown in the grouped frequency table. Height (cm): 30 < h ≤ 40 | 40 < h ≤ 50 | 50 < h ≤ 60 | 60 < h ≤ 70. Frequency: 15 | 14 | 12 | 11. To draw a frequency polygon, Omar plots the points (40, 15), (50, 14), (60, 12), (70, 11). Explain Omar's mistake and write down the points Omar should plot.
items.answer: Omar used the upper class boundaries; the points should be plotted at the midpoints: (35, 15), (45, 14), (55, 12), (65, 11).
items.markingKey: B1 midpoints not upper bounds; B1 correct points. [2]

items.stem: An isosceles trapezium has two angles of 80° at the ends of its longer parallel side. Work out the other two angles.
items.markingKey: Co-interior angles between the parallel sides add to 180° (M1); 100° (A1).

items.stem: Work out 0.3 × 4.
items.markingKey: 3 × 4 then place the decimal point: 1.2. [1]

items.stem: Simplify 8x²/4x.
items.markingKey: Divide numerator and denominator by the common factor 4x: 2x. [1]

items.stem: Tomás says the function x → 7 − x is its own inverse. Is Tomás correct? Explain.
items.answer: Yes. Applying it twice: x → 7 − x → 7 − (7 − x) = x, so it undoes itself.
items.markingKey: M1 applies twice or finds inverse; A1 conclusion. [2]

items.stem: Priya rolls a dice 600 times and gets a 6 on 100 rolls. Do the results suggest the dice is biased? Explain.
items.answer: Expected about 100 sixes for a fair dice. 100 is close to 100, so there is no strong evidence of bias.
items.markingKey: M1 expected frequency; A1 conclusion with comparison. [2]

items.stem: Triangle A has vertices (1, 0), (2, 2), (2, 3). Triangle A is enlarged by scale factor 4 with centre the origin. Write down the coordinates of the image.
items.markingKey: Vector from centre to each vertex × 4 (M1); image (4, 0), (8, 8), (8, 12) (A1).

items.stem: Elena drives 120 km at 60 km/h and then another 120 km at 90 km/h. Elena says the average speed for the whole journey is 75 km/h. Explain why Elena is wrong and find the correct average speed.
items.answer: More time is spent at the slower speed, so you cannot average the speeds. Total time = 2 + 1.333333 = 3.333333 h; average = 240 ÷ 3.333333 = 72 km/h.
items.markingKey: B1 explanation; B1 correct average using total distance ÷ total time. [2]

items.stem: The circumference of a circular flower bed is 15.7 m. Calculate its diameter, correct to 1 decimal place.
Find the equation of the line of points that are the same distance from (0, −6) and (0, 2).
items.markingKey: Midpoint of AB = (0, −2) (M1); AB is vertical so the bisector is horizontal: y = −2 (A1).

items.stem: Aisha says that x > 9 and x ≥ 10 describe the same set of numbers. Is this true if x must be an integer? Is it true if x can be any number? Explain.
items.answer: For integers, yes: both give 10, 11, …. For any number, no: x = 9.5 satisfies x > 9 but not x ≥ 10.
items.markingKey: B1 integer case; B1 counter-example for real numbers. [2]

items.stem: Design a data collection sheet that could be used in an investigation into whether Stage 9 boys are taller than Stage 9 girls.
items.answer: A table with columns for heights of boys and girls (and a tally/frequency column if grouped), with space for each person or item.
items.markingKey: B1 suitable headings; B1 suitable categories or groups / space for values. [2]

items.stem: Daniel says: "5⁵ × 2⁵ = 10⁵." Is Daniel correct? Explain.
items.markingKey: B1 correct decision; B1 reason with values or index law. [2]

items.stem: Find the equation of the line parallel to y = 4x + 6 that passes through (0, −3).
items.markingKey: Parallel lines have the same gradient, 4 (B1); −3 = 4 × 0 + c (M1); c = −3, y = 4x − 3 (A1).

items.stem: Without a calculator, work out 4/9 ÷ (5/8 + 2/3).
items.markingKey: bracket first: 31/24 (M1); then the remaining operation with a common denominator (M1); 32/93 (A1).

items.stem: Data from Lima show a strong positive correlation between the shoe size of children and the reading score of children. Leila says: "An increase in the shoe size of children causes an increase in the reading score of children." Explain why Leila may be wrong.
items.answer: Correlation does not prove causation. Both are probably affected by a third factor: the age of the children.
items.markingKey: B1 correlation is not causation; B1 suitable third factor. [2]

items.stem: A cylinder has radius 6 cm and height 10 cm. Calculate its volume, correct to 1 decimal place.
Zara says that a mass of 92 kg given to the nearest whole number could actually be 91.5 kg but could not be 92.5 kg. Explain why Zara is correct.
items.answer: 91.5 rounds up to 92, but 92.5 rounds up to the next value, 93. So 91.5 ≤ m < 92.5.
items.markingKey: B1 explains rounding at each bound; B1 inequality. [2]

items.stem: A rectangular field has length (3x + 2) m and width x m. (a) Write an expression for the perimeter of the field. Simplify your answer. (b) The perimeter is 52 m. Here are the first five terms of a sequence: 11, 12.5, 14, 15.5, 17. Find the nth term.

Felix takes a bus and then a train to school. The probability the bus is on time is 0.9. The probability the train is on time is 0.65. The events are independent. (a) Work out the probability that both are on time. (b) Work out the probability that both are late. (c) Work out the probability that at least one of them is late. (d) There are 190 school days. On how many days would you expect both to be on time?

A boat leaves harbour H and sails 4 km due west to point B, then 4 km due south to point C. (a) Calculate the direct distance from C back to H, to 2 decimal places. (b) Explain why angle BCH is 45°. (c) A scale drawing uses 1 cm to represent 1 km. How long is the line HB on the drawing? (d) Write down the bearing of B from H.
items.answer: (a) 5.66 km (b) Triangle HBC is right-angled at B and isosceles (HB = BC), so the other two angles are each 45°. (c) 4 cm (d) 270°

items.stem: A building company estimates that 8 workers take 24 days to complete a job. Each worker is paid $95 per day. (a) How many days would 12 workers take, working at the same rate? items.markingKey: (a) M1 8 × 24 = 192 worker-days; A1 [2] (b) M1 192 worker-days × 95; A1 [2] (c) M1; A1 [2]

A cuboid measures 3 cm by 4 cm by 12 cm. (a) Calculate the length of the diagonal of the 3 cm by 4 cm base. (b) Calculate the length of the longest straight rod that fits inside the cuboid (from one corner to the opposite corner).

Noah asks members of a football club which sport is the most popular in the school. Noah asks 10 people the question "Most people prefer cats. Which pet do you prefer?" (a) Give two reasons why the results may be biased. (b) Rewrite the question so that it is not biased. (c) Describe how to choose a better sample.
items.answer: (a) Football club members are likely to choose football. Also the question: The first sentence influences the answer. (b) Which of these pets do you prefer? Cat / Dog / Fish / Other / None (c) Choose a random sample from the whole school register.
items.markingKey: (a) B1 B1 [2] (b) B1 neutral wording; B1 suitable response options [2] (c) B1 B1 [2]

items.markingKey: Improper fractions 11/3, 3/2, 9/4 (M1); multiply by reciprocals for ÷ (M1); 2 4/9 (A1).

items.stem: The back-to-back stem-and-leaf diagram shows the marks of students in two classes in a mathematics test. Class A leaves are on the left and Class B leaves are on the right. 4 | 3 |; 4 0 | 4 | 8; 3 2 | 5 | 1 2 5 6; 7 6 5 4 3 1 0 | 6 | 2 6 9; 7 | 7 | 0 1 2 3 5 8; | 8 | 1. Key: 0 | 6 | 2 means 60 marks for Class A and 62 marks for Class B. (a) Find the median for Class A. (b) Which group did better on average? Give a reason. (c) Which group is more consistent? Give a reason. (d) How many members of Class A had a value of 61 or more?
items.answer: (a) 61 (b) Class B: it has the higher median (Class A 61, Class B 69). (c) Class B: it has the smaller range (33). (d) 7
items.markingKey: (a) M1 position; A1 [2] (b) B1 group; B1 reason [2] (c) B1 [1] (d) B1 [1]

items.stem: A cuboid measures 4 cm by 3 cm by 5 cm. (a) Describe the net of the cuboid: how many rectangles, and of what sizes? (b) Work out the total area of the net. (c) Describe the plan view of the cuboid when it stands on its 4 × 3 face. (d) Describe the front elevation when viewed from the 4 cm side. (e) Write down the number of edges and vertices.
items.answer: (a) 6 rectangles: two 4 × 3, two 4 × 5, two 3 × 5 (b) 94 cm² (c) A rectangle 4 cm by 3 cm (d) A rectangle 4 cm by 5 cm (e) 12 edges, 8 vertices

items.markingKey: Direct proportion. [1]

items.stem: Write down what is meant by independent events.
items.answer: The outcome of one does not affect the probability of the other.

items.stem: Without dividing, explain why 1/20 is a terminating decimal but 1/140 is a recurring decimal.
items.answer: 20 has only 2 and 5 as prime factors, so it divides a power of 10. 140 = 20 × 7 has the prime factor 7, which does not divide any power of 10, so the decimal recurs.
items.markingKey: B1 prime factors 2 and 5 only terminate; B1 other prime factor gives recurring. [2]

items.stem: Complete the table of values for y = x² − 2 for x = −3, −2, −1, 0, 1, 2, 3.
Explain why a position-to-term rule is more useful than a term-to-term rule for finding the 100th term.
items.answer: With a position-to-term rule you substitute n = 100 directly; with a term-to-term rule you must work out all 99 previous terms.

items.stem: The height of a tree, h m, is measured as 100 m to the nearest 10. Complete the inequality: … ≤ h < …
items.markingKey: B1 lower bound 95; B1 upper bound 105 with correct inequality signs.

items.markingKey: 1 hectares = 10,000 m². [1]

items.markingKey: √(4/9) = 2/3, a fraction. The others are irrational. [1]

items.stem: Explain why x + y = 6 and 2x + 2y = 12 do not have a single solution.
items.answer: The second equation is just the first multiplied by 2, so they are the same line; every point on it is a solution.
items.markingKey: B1 same line / equivalent; B1 infinitely many solutions. [2]

items.stem: A website records the number of downloads, in hundreds, each week for 5 weeks. week 1: 78, week 2: 79, week 3: 82, week 4: 80, week 5: 88. Calculate the 3-point moving averages. Give your answers to 1 decimal place.
items.markingKey: M1 (78 + 79 + 82) ÷ 3; A1 all 3 correct.

items.stem: Ethan says: "The diagonals of a rectangle are perpendicular." Is Ethan correct? Give a reason.
items.answer: No. Only when the rectangle is a square; e.g. a 6 cm by 2 cm rectangle has diagonals that are not at 90°.
items.markingKey: B1 decision; B1 reason or counter-example. [2]

items.stem: A pattern is made from tiles. Pattern n has 3 tiles in each of n rows plus 6 extra tiles. Write a formula for the total number of tiles, T, in pattern n.

What stays the same in a reflection, rotation or translation?
options: Lengths and angles (the shapes are congruent)
items.answer: Lengths and angles (the shapes are congruent)

items.stem: Ana is investigating whether students who sleep more get higher test scores. Explain why the question "Is this a good topic?" would not be a useful question to ask, and suggest a better one.
items.answer: It is vague and will not give data that can be analysed. A better question asks for specific data on hours of sleep and test scores, with clear answer options or a number.
items.markingKey: B1 reason (vague / not measurable); B1 improved specific question. [2]

items.stem: Amara mixes paint in the ratio red : white = 2 : 3. Arjun mixes red : white = 3 : 4. Whose paint is redder? Explain.
items.answer: Amara: red is 2/5 = 40% of the paint; Arjun: 3/7 = 42.9%. Arjun's paint is redder.
items.markingKey: M1 compares fractions of red (common form); A1 conclusion. [2]

items.stem: A bag contains 6 yellow, 2 white and 3 black balls. One ball is taken at random. Work out the probability that it is yellow or black.
items.markingKey: Mutually exclusive: P(yellow) + P(black) = 6/11 + 3/11 (M1) = 9/11 (A1).

items.stem: Arjun says that dividing 59 by 0.5 gives a smaller answer than 59. Explain why Arjun is wrong, using fractions.
items.answer: 0.5 = 1/2; dividing by 1/2 is the same as multiplying by 2, so 59 ÷ 0.5 = 118, which is larger.
items.markingKey: B1 reciprocal; B1 value. [2]

items.stem: Mateo leaves home at 10:00. A distance-time graph of the journey shows: a straight line from (0 min, 0 km) to (40 min, 8 km); a horizontal line for 20 minutes; a straight line to 18 km over the next 30 minutes; then a straight line back to home taking 60 minutes. Calculate the speed, in km/h, on the way back home.
items.markingKey: 18 km in 60 min (M1); 18 km/h (A1).

items.stem: Here are the first five terms of a sequence: 20, 29, 38, 47, 56. Find the nth term.
items.markingKey: Common difference 9 (M1); 9n + (20 − 9) = 9n + 11 (A1).

items.stem: Ana works out 1.93 × 10⁻¹. Freya works out 1.93 ÷ 10¹. Will they get the same answer? Explain.
items.answer: Yes. 10⁻¹ = 1/10¹, so multiplying by 10⁻¹ is the same as dividing by 10¹. Both get 0.193.
items.markingKey: B1 equivalence explained; B1 value. [2]

items.stem: A coin has radius 8 mm. Work out its area, giving your answer in terms of π.
items.markingKey: A = πr² (M1); 64π mm² (A1).

items.answer: The power should be 8, not −8; the number is greater than 1. Correct: 2.03 × 10⁸.
items.markingKey: B1 reason (the power should be 8, not −8; the number is greater than 1); B1 2.03 × 10⁸. [2]

items.markingKey: M1 median is value number 5.5; A1 27; B1 range 44.

items.stem: Priya says a solid with straight edges has 11 faces, 7 vertices and 17 edges. Use Euler's formula to decide whether this is possible.
items.answer: F + V − E = 11 + 7 − 17 = 1. This is not 2, so the solid cannot exist.
items.markingKey: M1 substitution; A1 conclusion. [2]

items.stem: Multiply out the brackets and simplify: (a + 4)(a − 1).
items.markingKey: Four products: 1a², −1a, 4a, −4 (M1); collect like terms: a² + 3a − 4 (A1).

items.stem: Lines AB and CD are parallel, with A and C on the left. A straight line EF crosses AB at P and CD at Q, with E above AB and F below CD. Angle APQ = 124°. Zara says angle CQP is also 124° because they are alternate angles. Explain the mistake and give the correct size of angle CQP.
items.answer: APQ and CQP are on the same side of the transversal, between the parallel lines: they are co-interior, so they add up to 180°. CQP = 56°.
items.markingKey: B1 identifies co-interior (not alternate); B1 180° − a. [2]

items.stem: A rectangle measures 6 cm by 6 cm. It is enlarged by scale factor 2. (a) Work out the dimensions of the image. (b) Work out the perimeter of the image and compare it with the original perimeter. (c) Work out the area of the image and compare it with the original area. items.answer: (a) 12 cm by 12 cm (b) 48 cm; it is 2 times the original 24 cm (c) 144 cm²; 4 times the original 36 cm² (d) Enlargement keeps the shape the same (similar shapes); only the lengths change.

items.stem: Chloe uses these response boxes for a question about dollars spent on snacks per week: 1–2, 2–3, 3–4. Identify two problems with the boxes and write a better set of boxes.
items.answer: The boxes overlap (e.g. 2 is in two boxes) and there is no box for values above 4 or below 1. Better: 1 up to but not including 2; 2 up to but not including 3; 3 up to but not including 4; 4 or more; less than 1.
items.markingKey: B1 overlap; B1 gaps/not exhaustive; B1 non-overlapping exhaustive set.

items.stem: Diego drives 360 km from Lima to the coast at an average driving speed of 90 km/h, with one stop of 20 minutes. The car travels 14 km per litre of fuel. items.stem: Tariq says the interior angles of a heptagon add up to 7 × 180° = 1260° because it can be split into 7 triangles. Explain the mistake and give the correct total.
items.answer: Joining one vertex to all the others splits the heptagon into 5 triangles, not 7, so the sum is (7 − 2) × 180° = 900°. (Splitting from a centre point gives 7 triangles but the 360° at the centre must be subtracted.)

items.markingKey: B1 bounds for each number; B1 conclusion. [2]

items.stem: A bag has 9 yellow and 3 white counters. A counter is taken at random and replaced, then a second counter is taken. Use a tree diagram to work out the probability that both counters are the same colour.
items.markingKey: Tree diagram with (9/12, 3/12) on both sets of branches (M1); (9/12)² + (3/12)² (M1) = 5/8 (A1).

items.stem: Write down the answer to 2.5 × 0.4.
items.markingKey: 25 × 4 = 100, two decimal places → 1.00. B1 [1]

items.stem: Write down the coordinates of the lowest point of the graph of y = x² + 4.
Arjun's sequence has nth term 5n + 3. Sofia's sequence has nth term 8n − 9. Explain why Sofia's terms will eventually be larger than Arjun's, and find the first position where this happens.
items.answer: Sofia's sequence increases by 8 each time, Arjun's by 5, so Sofia's catches up. 8n − 9 > 5n + 3 when n > 4, so first at n = 5.
items.markingKey: B1 compares differences; B1 first position. [2]

items.stem: A taxi in Colombo charges $5 to start and then $0.60 per kilometre. Write a formula for the fare, F dollars, for a journey of k kilometres, and use it to find the fare for 10 km.
Noah shares $65 in the ratio 2 : 3 and says the first share is $32.50. Explain the mistake and find both shares.
items.answer: Noah divided by 2 instead of by the total number of parts (5). 1 part = 65 ÷ 5 = $13; shares $26 and $39.
items.markingKey: B1 must divide by total parts; B1 correct shares. [2]

items.stem: A virus has a length of about 0.00012 mm. Write this number in standard form.
In a stem-and-leaf diagram, the key is 8 | 1 means 8.1 m. What value does 5 | 2 represent?
items.markingKey: Stem 5, leaf 2: 5.2 m. [1]

items.stem: What fraction of a full circle is a sector with angle 36°?
Omar rotates the point (4, 5) through 90° clockwise about the origin and gets (−5, 4). Explain the mistake and give the correct image.
items.answer: (−5, 4) is the result of a 90° ANTICLOCKWISE rotation. Clockwise: (x, y) → (y, −x), giving (5, −4).
items.markingKey: B1 direction confused; B1 correct image. [2]

items.stem: Nadia wants to solve 2x + y = 11 and x + 2y = −5 by elimination. Explain what Nadia should do first, and why.
items.answer: Multiply the equations so that the coefficients of x (or y) are equal, e.g. first × 1 and second × 2, then subtract to eliminate x. (Solution x = 9, y = −7.)
items.markingKey: B1 multiply to make coefficients equal; B1 then add/subtract to eliminate one variable. [2]

items.stem: A school in Nairobi has 390 boys and 180 girls. Mateo takes a sample of 38 students in proportion to the size of each group. How many boys and how many girls should be in the sample?
Two lines are crossed by a transversal. A pair of corresponding angles are 87° and 91°. Aisha says the two lines are parallel. Explain why Aisha is wrong.
items.answer: If the lines were parallel the corresponding angles would be equal. They are not equal, so the lines are not parallel.
items.markingKey: B1 corresponding angles equal for parallel lines; B1 conclusion. [2]

items.stem: The points (1, 3), (5, 3), (5, 7), (1, 7) are joined in order. Name the quadrilateral formed and give one property that confirms your answer.
items.markingKey: B1 correct name; B1 property supported by the coordinates (side lengths, parallel sides, right angles or symmetry).

items.stem: Without a calculator, work out 3/4 + 2/5 × 5/12.
items.markingKey: 2/5 × 5/12 = 1/6 first (M1); then the remaining operation with a common denominator (M1); 11/12 (A1).

items.stem: Ravi and Ethan each throw the same drawing pin to estimate the probability it lands point up. Ravi throws it 10 times and Ethan throws it 500 times. Whose estimate is more reliable? Explain.
items.answer: Ethan's: more trials give a more reliable estimate of the probability (relative frequency settles down as the number of trials increases).
items.markingKey: B1 decision; B1 reason. [2]

items.stem: Calculate 3.7 ÷ 10² without a calculator.
items.markingKey: ÷ 10² is the same as ÷ 100 (M1); 0.037 (A1).

items.stem: Sipho says the point (2, 5) lies on the line y = 4x − 4. Show how to check whether Sipho is right.
items.answer: Substitute x = 2: y = 4 × 2 − 4 = 4. This is not 5, so the point does not lie on the line.
items.markingKey: M1 substitution; A1 conclusion. [2]

items.stem: A function maps x to 4x + 6. The output is 14. Work out the input.
items.markingKey: 4x + 6 = 14 or use the inverse (M1); x = 2 (A1).

items.stem: (x + 2)(x + p) = x² + 9x + q. Find the values of p and q.
items.markingKey: M1 expands to x² + (2 + p)x + 2p, so 2 + p = 9; A1 p = 7; A1 q = 2 × 7 = 14.

items.stem: 5 workers take 12 days to build a wall. Samuel says that with 10 workers it would take 24 days. Explain why Samuel is wrong and give the correct answer.
items.answer: This is inverse proportion: doubling the workers halves the days. It would take 6 days.
items.markingKey: B1 inverse proportion; B1 correct value. [2]

items.stem: Work out the value of 10⁻³, giving your answer as a fraction.

A farmer weighed 30 apples. The mass of each apple is m grams. The results are shown in the grouped frequency table. Mass (g): 80 < m ≤ 100 | 100 < m ≤ 120 | 120 < m ≤ 140. Frequency: 15 | 5 | 10. To draw a frequency polygon, Felix plots the points (100, 15), (120, 5), (140, 10). Explain Felix's mistake and write down the points Felix should plot.
items.answer: Felix used the upper class boundaries; the points should be plotted at the midpoints: (90, 15), (110, 5), (130, 10).
items.markingKey: B1 midpoints not upper bounds; B1 correct points. [2]

items.stem: A rectangular swimming pool in Riyadh is 12 m long and 8 m wide. The water is 1.5 m deep everywhere. (a) Work out the volume of water in m³. (b) Work out the volume of water in litres. (c) Water is pumped in at 500 litres per minute. How many hours does it take to fill the pool? Give your answer to 1 decimal place.
Triangle A has vertices (3, 4), (3, 1), (1, 1). Triangle A is enlarged by scale factor 4 with centre (0, 1). Write down the coordinates of the image.
items.markingKey: Vector from centre to each vertex × 4 (M1); image (12, 13), (12, 1), (4, 1) (A1).

items.stem: Grace hires a bike in Istanbul. There is a fixed charge of $5 and then $4.00 per hour. Grace has $80 to spend. Let h be the number of whole hours. (a) Write an inequality in h. (b) Solve the inequality 5 + 4h ≤ 80. (c) Write down the greatest number of whole hours Grace can hire the bike for. (d) Show the solution set for h on a number line, in words.
items.answer: (a) 5 + 4h ≤ 80 (b) h ≤ 18.75 (c) 18 (d) Closed circle at 18.75, line to the left down to 0.
items.markingKey: (a) B1 [1] (b) M1 4h ≤ 75; A1 [2] (c) B1 rounds down [1] (d) B1 [1]

items.stem: Jonas is investigating whether a six-sided dice is biased. (a) Write a hypothesis for the investigation. (b) State the data that needs to be collected and whether it is primary or secondary. (c) Jonas uses a sample of size 100. Give one reason why this is better than a sample of size 10. (d) Describe one problem that could happen when collecting the data, and how to reduce it.
items.answer: (a) The dice lands on 6 more often than on the other numbers. (b) the score on each roll; primary data (c) A larger sample is more reliable / representative and reduces the effect of unusual values. (d) e.g. people give inaccurate answers / measurements are inaccurate; use clear questions, repeat measurements, use a larger random sample.
items.markingKey: (a) B1 [1] (b) B1 data; B1 type [2] (c) B1 [1] (d) B1 problem; B1 solution [2]

items.stem: A ladder 8 m long leans against a vertical wall in Lagos. The foot of the ladder is 2 m from the base of the wall on horizontal ground. (a) Calculate how high up the wall the ladder reaches, to 2 decimal places. (b) Safety rules say the height should be about 4 times the distance from the wall. Is the ladder safe? Explain. (c) The foot of the ladder slips until the top is 0.3 m lower down the wall. Calculate the new distance of the foot from the wall, to 2 decimal places.
Work out the number of faces, edges and vertices of a triangular prism, and show that they satisfy Euler's formula F + V − E = 2.
items.markingKey: B1 faces; B1 edges and vertices; B1 Euler check 5 + 6 − 9 = 2.

items.stem: This question is about the fraction 5/6 and the recurring decimal 0.818181…. (a) Write 5/6 as a decimal. (b) Write 0.818181… as a fraction in its simplest form. (c) Which is larger, 5/6 or 0.818181…? Show how you decide. (d) Work out 5/6 + 0.818181… as a fraction.
items.markingKey: (a) B1 [1] (b) M1 100x − x; A1 [2] (c) M1 compare in same form; A1 [2] (d) M1 common denominator; A1 [2]

items.stem: A spinner has four colours. The table gives probabilities: P(red) = 0.3, P(blue) = 0.15, P(green) = x, P(yellow) = 0.25. (a) Work out the value of x. (b) Work out the probability that the spinner lands on red or blue. (c) The spinner is spun 200 times. How many times would you expect it to land on green?

Yusuf has $10,000 to invest for 3 years. Bank A pays 6% compound interest per year. Bank B pays 6% simple interest per year. (a) Calculate the value of the investment in Bank A after 3 years. (b) Calculate the value in Bank B after 3 years. (c) In Bank A, after how many whole years will the investment first be worth more than $12,500.00?

Mateo leaves home at 10:00. A distance-time graph of the journey shows: a straight line from (0 min, 0 km) to (20 min, 20 km); a horizontal line for 10 minutes; a straight line to 26 km over the next 20 minutes; then a straight line back to home taking 60 minutes. Calculate the speed, in km/h, for the third part of the journey.
items.markingKey: 6 km in 20 min (M1); 18 km/h (A1).

items.stem: Lucas is investigating the expression 56n + 12 where n is a whole number. (a) Factorise the expression completely. (b) Use your factorisation to explain why the value is always a multiple of 4. (c) Work out the value when n = 4 and check that it is a multiple of 4.
items.markingKey: (a) M1; A1 [2] (b) B1 [1] (c) M1 substitution; A1 value shown as a multiple [2]

items.stem: Use trial and improvement to find ∛691 correct to 1 decimal place. Show your trials.

A bakery in Hanoi records the number of loaves it sells each week for 10 weeks. week 1: 56, week 2: 58, week 3: 58, week 4: 67, week 5: 66, week 6: 71, week 7: 76, week 8: 82, week 9: 83, week 10: 91. (a) Calculate the 3-point moving averages, to 1 decimal place. (b) Describe the trend. (c) In week 11 the value is 95. Work out the next 3-point moving average, to 1 decimal place.

ABCD is a parallelogram with A(−3, −1), B(5, 5) and C(4, 13). (a) Find the midpoint of the diagonal AC. (b) The diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other. Use this to find the coordinates of D. (c) Point P lies on AB so that AP : PB = 3 : 1. Find the coordinates of P.
items.markingKey: (a) M1; A1 [2] (b) M1 midpoint of BD = midpoint of AC; A1 [2] (c) M1 3/4 of the way; A1 [2]

items.stem: Solve 3(x + 4) = 33.
items.markingKey: Expand 3x + 12 = 33 or divide by 3 (M1); x = 7 (A1).

items.stem: Find the equation of the line of points that are the same distance from (4, 2) and (8, 2).
items.markingKey: Midpoint of AB = (6, 2) (M1); AB is horizontal so the bisector is vertical: x = 6 (A1).
